primary_source_support.title: Grinnell College Musical Instrument Collection: violoncello
primary_source_support.support: Documents the modern cello construction, seated support, floor peg, fingerboard stopping and bow hand.
primary_source_support.limits: Describes its collection instrument and normal interface, not all techniques or variants.

primary_source_support.title: Grinnell College Musical Instrument Collection: double bass
primary_source_support.support: Documents the bass endpin, standing/high-stool interface and separate bowing/plucking and fingering functions.
primary_source_support.limits: Collection-based construction and normal playing description; no universal exact height or angle.

primary_source_support.title: All Newton Music School: The String Family
primary_source_support.support: Independent music-school account of cello/bass support and typical hand roles.
primary_source_support.limits: Introductory text; unrelated broad claims on the page were not adopted.

primary_source_support.title: Internet Cello Society: Conversation with Gerhard Mantel, Tim Janof
primary_source_support.support: Primary interview expressly discusses bow-hair contact-point adjustments near the bridge and flexible posture.
primary_source_support.limits: Technique advice is not treated as a universal required posture or contact point.

primary_source_support.title: Brinton Smith: Feuermann filmed-performance analysis, chapter 4
primary_source_support.support: Primary performance analysis separates projected vertical appearance, instrument/body angles and player-dependent posture.
primary_source_support.limits: Observational study of selected filmed players, not an exhaustive pose taxonomy.

primary_source_support.title: Yamaha: How to Play the Violin — Bowing
primary_source_support.support: Adjacent family evidence distinguishes strings and the basic bow area between fingerboard and bridge.
primary_source_support.limits: Violin instruction corroborates geometry; not used alone to prove cello technique. Its broad always-bowed phrase is not adopted.

primary_source_support.title: Yamaha: Instruments related to the violin — The cello
primary_source_support.support: Documents historical changes and endpin adoption, supporting preservation of the current explicit endpin specialization.
primary_source_support.limits: Historical variants do not mandate broadening this profile.

primary_source_support.title: Philharmonia: Cello
primary_source_support.support: Original ledger source remains available; its current text discusses bowing and material variants.
primary_source_support.limits: Current extracted prose does not by itself establish all ledger posture abstractions. No source-video examination claimed.

primary_source_support.title: Philharmonia: Double Bass
primary_source_support.support: Original ledger source remains available and identifies the largest orchestral string instrument and differing bow grips.
primary_source_support.limits: Current extracted prose does not by itself establish all ledger standing/high-stool abstractions. No source-video examination claimed.

deduplication_and_exclusions: The four prior KEEP candidates are cello_seated_bowing_action, double_bass_floor_play_action, cello_endpin_bowed_prop and double_bass_human_scale_prop. Complete current rows match the prior saved rows; they are repeated coverage, not newly discovered improvements.
Six nearby/context rows are not six additional physical defects or instrument profiles. Generic non-instrument uses of bowing, such as image distortion, are outside scope.
The prior hand-role correction concerns a shared wind pose and trumpet action; its changes are not attributed to this audit.
The known object-versus-playing routing/ownership problem remains prior deferred scope work. It was neither resolved nor reclassified as a fresh cello/bass finding.
limits: KEEP concerns the selected complete physical meanings. It does not certify all instrument variants, general routing, bilingual retrieval, final-prompt exposure, adoption, performance quality, or rendering.

Cello bridge-region wording locates bow contact on strings; it does not require rubbing the wooden bridge or all strings simultaneously. Fingerboard and opposing-hand context constrain the regional neck wording.
Upright/vertical language is not an exact image-axis or numerical-angle constraint. Complete instrument scale includes body, long neck and support; no pixel deformation finding was measured.
The original Philharmonia prose does not by itself establish all posture abstractions, and no source-video examination is claimed. Independent Grinnell/All Newton support is bounded to this audit.
Inventory/test associations are not proof of production adoption. No actual AFTER CLI, retrieval, consumer selection, prompt or image-quality outcome was measured.
No source edits, runtime executions, tests, or generated images formed part of this audit or this derivative.
